paper_reference: Industrial IIoT hybrid wireless system for CNC machining factory floors. Li-Fi (850 nm IR, ceiling-mount, DCO-OFDM) provides the primary high-density downlink per work cell. Co-exists with Wi-Fi 6 (5 GHz OFDMA, mobility/general IT) and 5G URLLC (n78 3.5 GHz, <1 ms safety E-stop). Simulation scope: Li-Fi optical PHY only. Wi-Fi 6 and 5G modeled as metadata/handoff thresholds. Key factory stressors: (1) Industrial dust + coolant aerosol → Beer-Lambert attenuation; (2) Metal-surface multipath (CNC beds, enclosures, rho~0.65); (3) High ambient illuminance from industrial LED ceiling fixtures (500 lux); (4) CNC servo/VFD EMI → strong 100 Hz mains flicker (mains_flicker_depth=0.10) and switching noise up to 20 kHz; (5) Vibration-induced RX misalignment (rx_tilt_deg=5); (6) Elevated temperature (318 K / 45 C). Hybrid handoff logic (not simulated): Li-Fi primary -> Wi-Fi 6 fallback on device mobility -> 5G URLLC for safety-critical control. One ceiling AP covers ~3 m radius at 5 m height with 30-degree half-angle beam. Target: 20 Mbps per cell, BER < 1e-4 after LDPC.
